notes.title: First Major Update: Artwork & Combat
notes.notes:
[p]\[u]\[b]Bug Fixes\[/b]\[/u]
[/p][p]- The invisible monster in the Ashen Roost has been replaced with a new machine-type enemy. This fixes that bug while also further increasing the player's chances of finding a Thaumetic Battery to power the lower floors.
[/p][p]- The Ashbury Arena fight is supposed to heal the party before each round but it was not healing the party for the first round. This has been fixed.
[/p][p]- There was a bug at the Abandoned Farmhouse that if a player tried to hide in shadows just as they were about to get caught, they could be teleported to a location farther ahead in the game. This has been fixed.
[/p][p]- The Scan feature from the Lore Book item was bugged out. The Scan mechanic has been rewritten and now works properly.
[/p][p]- The Shoulder Canon (MK-I) device had a bug that caused Knockdown to persist until combat ended. This has been fixed.
[/p][p]- Very rarely a NaN value gets returned for a character's HP value. A new script has been implemented to catch all damage and healing to check for any "Not a number" values before applying HP changes. 

[/p][p]\[u]\[b]Content Update\[/b]\[/u]
[/p][p]- Slowly but surely, pixel by pixel, I have gotten the new battlers ready. I am pleased to report that the default asset battlers have finally been replaced with the custom artwork I've been steadily working on for the past few months. My next artistic endeavor (at some point) will be to bring the clashing map tilesets closer together towards a more uniform look.
[/p][p]- Iconography has been updated in an effort to bring the game's overall look into a more uniform style.
[/p][p]- Damage pop-ups now include the element or damage type of the hit.
[/p][p]- Magitech Blasters and Magitech Rifles have been changed. The old way had players button-mashing to either cast one skill or max out the bar and cast a different skill. This was clunky and counter-intuitive. Blasters and Rifles now activate their different skills in a new way. A window will appear with keypad combos to any known Blaster/Rifle skills. Players will get up to 10 seconds to input a short key combo (like up, up, down, etc) to select which skill they want to continue with.
[/p][p]- All damage over time and regeneration effects have been reworked. A new combat controller will handle these effects.
[/p][p]- Several various updates to the UI for smoother look and better readability.
[/p][p]- The tutorial images have been updated. Some new tutorial images have been added.
[/p][p]- There is now an option in the party menu called "Info" that will allow players to revisit the tutorial information.
[/p][p]- The Scan mechanic has been rewritten. Using the Lore Book or the Scan ability now reveals enemy weaknesses and shows a visual HP bar for the duration of the fight.

[/p][p]\[u]\[b]In Progress & Coming Soon\[/b]\[/u]
[/p][p]- Now that the new artwork is in place, I am getting together the up-to-date screenshots needed to redo the tutorial images.
[/p][p]- Also getting together up-to-date screenshots for the Steam store page.[/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Patch of the Wolf: Bug Fixes
notes.notes:
Thanks to the YouTube channel Slice of Kris, I was finally able to track down the missing graphic bug for Ellessidel.


[u][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/u]


- I do believe the long-elusive missing graphic bug for Ellessidel has finally been fixed. Ellessidel should no longer turn invisible when she loses her temper. 


- The worgs Bawz and Koda were displaying the wrong portrait in battle. This has been fixed.


- Ogin's battle portrait has been fixed as well.


- The boss rage bar was showing in regular fights during Natasha's escape. This has been fixed.


- Some enemies had their elemental weaknesses offset by 1 in the database. This was causing odd vulnerabilities like earth-type enemies being weak against Lightning when it should be Air. These enemies have been updated.


- Several Light Armor items were displaying General Armor tooltips. These items have been updated.


- All Shield tooltips have been updated and the Light Shield tooltips have been rewritten to better communicate their function.


- For some reason Marrick's face graphic as a kid got overwritten. This also happened with an old character emote file that cause Natasha's kid character to display a graphical bug during the scene just before she wakes up at the campfire. These have been repaired.


- The Energy Drain state was not supposed to persist after battle. This has been fixed.


- The Rotwood Giant battle had a typo and was playing the wrong battle music. This fight has been corrected.


- Vanessa was present in the party when Marrick starts his solo part. This has been fixed.


- The northern entrance to the Norfolk Caves was mislabeled. It now says the correct zone name.


- There were magic fishtanks floating around randomly during a scene for some reason. They have been re-installed properly.

- There was a rock that looked out-of-place in the Old Logging Road. It has been removed to avoid the understandable confusion that it was important.

- Characters that are removed from the party permanently due to the story are automatically unequipped so that the player does not lose items. This was not working for one particular character but it has been fixed.

- Some debug events that were not supposed to be active have been removed.



[u][b]Content Update[/b][/u]


- I thought it was going to take longer to post my next update but thanks to Mr. Slice of Kris I was able to finally fix the Ellessidel bug that had been eluding me for a while. It really messes up the impact of a scene and makes a certain ability no fun to use so it was important enough to get out a hotfix.

- I am in the midst of some exciting upgrades. Players may notice some slight graphical changes in battle. This was done in preparation for the first round of artwork updates. I realized I am going to have to "git gud" at pixel art if I want to continue as a solo dev with a low budget. Cultivating these skills will also expand my game dev abilities and give me full control over the quality of the next game (as well as expand my options for future projects). 

- Enemies and battle backgrounds have been processed in preparation for the new character battlers I am working on.

- The Misty Marshes has been changed so that players can return to the inner marshes if they so choose.

- Still actively working on remaining bug reports. Can't stop, won't stop   :)




More to come. I just wanted to get the big ones out of the way as quickly as possible.

notes.title: Streamer Update: Content & Fixes
notes.notes:
I've been up for almost 50 hours... but it was worth it. I noticed a streamer on YouTube had given Neverspring a try and so I watched all 6 hours and took notes on the bugs and hard points. The guy was an absolute champion, some of the stuff I saw him running into was jaw-dropping so I figured I could sleep when I'm dead lol.

I was able to get a chunk done but there's still more to do, along with the currently active reports (some of which I was able to get to in this update as well).



[u][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/u]


- Some typos have been fixed.


- The missing tooltip for Support Drones has been fixed.


- The tooltip for Casual Shoes has been rewritten to better explain that it enables dash for faster walk speed.


- The slimes in the Lower Sewers were 4 levels higher than they should be. This has been fixed.


- Some trinket accessories were missing their promised Max HP increase. These have been updated.


- The invisible monster in the Misty Marshes has been removed.


- The daggers were all displaying their tooltips as swords. This has been fixed.


- Dunkargo's starting level had not been changed to reflect the changes in the recent difficulty patch. His starting level has been updated.


- The boss rage bar was filling too fast. It has been tweaked to fill slower.


- There was a bug that locked out Magitech Blasters and Magitech Rifles in the shop. This has been fixed.


- Some items were selling for an old currency that would show up as "deleted item". These items have had their prices corrected.


- The little Roden-Lago merchant in the Misty Marshes was selling a couple discontinued items. These have been removed.


- Andorlane's scene introducing Gafgaren showed the wrong scrolling background. This has been fixed.


- The Sanctum's enemy encounter chance was higher than it was supposed to be. It has been changed to normal levels.


- The Item Merchants were stuck on old data and selling items for more gold than they were supposed to be. Players will notice a drop in Item Merchant prices to bring them in line with other stores and vending machines.


- Food Rations have been added to some shops and vending machines.



[u][b]Content Update[/b][/u]


- The shop screen was clunky, confusing, and needed to communicate stat changes better. It has been upgraded with a new experimental shop screen that will be improved further in future updates.


- An old game mechanic that was cut before release has been reactivated. As long as Marrick is in the party (or any thief class character), the player can hide in shadows. Observant players may see noticeably dark areas that can be used to hide. Players need only step into the shadowy area to activate hiding. Stepping out of the shadows will bring the player out of hiding.


- The Abandoned Farmhouse has been updated. Players can now utilize the "hide in shadows" mechanic here.


- An old game mechanic that was cut before release has been reactivated. Enemies will reveal their damage type weaknesses in a more noticeable way by displaying an icon for any discovered weaknesses. If an enemy displays a "?" icon then they have a vulnerability that the player can discover and exploit. This was done to help guide players towards noticing the damage type mechanics. Some players were confused by moments of sudden damage changes because it was not communicated well enough that there are strengths and weaknesses in play for enemies.



[u][b]In Progress & Coming Soon[/b][/u]


- After watching gameplay from a couple streamers, I am bumping the Tutorial upgrade priority to the top of the list. I noticed players would either skip or forget the tutorial info at the beginning of the game. There are also some things that need to be added to the tutorial info. Some players are unaware that they can trigger combos, or run away from battles, or link magitech devices, etc. An option will be added to the party's main menu for players that wish to revisit the tutorial info.


- Right now the level up screen only appears when a character learns a new skill. This makes it also appear when a new magitech skill gets unlocked, even if the character did not level up. When that happens, it shows the character's stats with combat buffs included, making it sometimes appear like a character "leveled up" and lost some stats. The stats lost are from temporary in-combat effects that end when battle ends. So while it is not de-leveling the character it is making it appear like it is. The way it works right now is causing confusion so I will tweak it to be better.


- The "Attack Chain" indicator is going to be rewritten. I had coded it in a way that attached the timer to the framerate, thinking it would help it slow down if someone lagged but in practice it is causing the circle indicator to sometimes choke up and then fast-forward. This results in the circle indicator sometimes going way faster than it normally does. I am working on a fix for this.


- Also working on current feedback and bug reports.




Just a reminder to players: Steam has been getting better about flagging for auto-updates but since code changes are such a small file size, even when you change a lot of it, sometimes Steam doesn't send out the update right away. If you don't get the update, a quick "Verify File Integrity" will force an update no matter how small.

notes.title: Lugae Fortress Hotfix
notes.notes:
The upgrade to Lugae's Fortress had 2 doors that had transfer points off by 1 tile. This would trap players in a wall when using these doors.

The doors have fixed.

Also added in a quick check whenever the map loads just in case anyone boots up an old save file from before the upgrade and finds themselves loading into a wall or something.

This is a very small update so players may need to "Verify Game Files" to force an immediate update.

notes.title: Bug Fixes & Upgrade: Lugae's Fortress
notes.notes:
[u][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/u]


- The Moldy Spores skill was designed poorly. Some players would get stun-locked into a forever sleep/slow loop in early game when there weren't enough party members to absorb the effect. This has been fixed.


- There was a bug that could cause a player's game to slip into a different combat system. This combat system is fully functional but is not meant for the game in it's current state, so players may or may not have noticed this bug if it did not cause any other problems. If a player could see little face graphics in the upper right-hand corner of the battle screen to represent the turn order of allies and enemies then their game file was afflicted with this bug. I am still searching for the source of how the bug was happening but in the meantime I have re-written the function that toggles combat systems to no longer be able to access the secondary combat system as a temporary fix.


- Fixed a couple typos and missing name boxes.





[u][b]Content Update[/b][/u]


- Lugae's Fortress has been upgraded significantly.


- Some extra dialogue has been added in to further direct the player towards their goals.


- The ascent from the great hall to the top of the castle has been redesigned. The original map for Lugae's Fortress was somewhat of a walk-through because players are technically in disguise during this time, so a battle would give away their presence. Keeping that in mind, the level design of the upgrade sees players having to deactivate a series of security measures in order to reach Inquisitor Lugae.


- Some maps have been altered slightly to accommodate these changes.

notes.title: Minor Content Update: Sanctum & Ashen Roost
notes.notes:
[u][b]Minor Content Update[/b][/u]


- The Sanctum (dungeon) has been updated. As an older map, it was lacking in level design compared to newer maps. 


- The Ashen Roost (final dungeon) has been updated significantly. The tower now has two distinct phases rather than one long crawl. The dungeon as a whole is now much more interactive. A new item called "Thaumetic Battery" now has a chance to drop from machine and construct type enemies. There is also a chance to find them in junk piles.

notes.title: Content Update: Combat & Difficulty
notes.notes:
[u][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/u]


- A new script has been written to check for initialization errors on start-up. Some game data is only written at the start of new game. This background process will fire off when loading a save file and check for missing or undefined data and, if detected, will force a reinitialization. This should help older save files, especially Early Access ones, run smoother.


- A reminder to players attempting to load Early Access save files from before March of 2022: the [i]Phoenix Down[/i] update in 2022 marked the start of a complete rewrite of the entire game. Save files older than March of 2022 are not salvageable because they will attempt to access deactivated content and a completely different database.


- The skill mastery feature was not working properly. This has been fixed. Skills can once again level up the more you use them. Higher level skills cost less and deal more damage/healing.


- More code clean up efforts for improved performance.


[u][b]Content Updates[/b][/u]


- Fullscreen/Window mode has been upgraded. Pressing F4 still toggles between Fullscreen and Window mode but now there is also a new setting in the options/config menu. The game now remembers your Fullscreen/Window mode between play sessions.


- The enemy database has been updated. Enemies now have their own leveling system. They have been reworked to level up as the player progresses. This should help bolster their stats for a more challenging combat experience. 


- A new Difficulty setting has been added to the options/config menu. Increasing the difficulty will make enemies stronger. Right now this only effects enemies and combat but the system has been set up for future updates so that it will later effect overall gameplay in a more dynamic way. ([i]Planned Feature Example: Higher difficulties unlock new achievements, special challenge zones, expanded lore, etc[/i])


- Some UI elements have been updated. Most notably the party menu screen and the combat HUD.


[u][b]Works In Progress[/b][/u]


- The casual shoes are still undergoing changes so sprint/dash is still in the works.


- There is a problem with the Scan/Lore ability that is causing it not to work properly. This is still being fixed.


- Actively testing the combat upgrades. It's tough to do it solo since I made the game and I know all the enemy weaknesses and whatnot so please don't hesitate to leave feedback on whether the changes feel too weak or too strong. 


[u][b]Developer Notes[/b][/u]


- The combat balancing has been tricky. I moved the enemy levels and difficulty setting to the top of the priority list because as tweaks and fixes stacked up, the combat fell out of balance and became laughably easy throughout the second half of the game. Some players were able to beat some mid and late game bosses in just 1 turn cycle. 


- I already felt like the lack of challenge could taint a player's story experience (like face-rolling a boss then having to listen to it talk big after the fight lol) but when I saw that one player was able to beat the game in 11 to 12 hours I realized it was also shaving down the game's playtime considerably. 


- Just for comparison, on a walk-through test where I can walk through walls and skip every fight it takes about 9 or 10 hours. So having the combat become so trivial was a problem that needed to be fixed right away.


- I apologize for the string of back-to-back updates. I try to fix any reported bugs as fast as possible and so I wind up posting fixes and requests as they come. I just can't stand the idea that someone might pay money for a game and then it sits there with a known bug for weeks/months. It just feels wrong so I try not to let it happen if I can. Thank you to everyone who has played so far! The feedback and bug reports have been invaluable. 





Just a reminder to all players! Sometimes Steam does not give an automatic update if it is too small. Code change updates don't do much to the file size so if you're ever in doubt, simply verify your game files. It will force an update, no matter how small, and you can be confident you have the most up-to-date version.

notes.title: Minor Update w/Hotfix
notes.notes:
[u][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/u]

- There was a bug that was putting Natasha as a kid into the party along with Natasha when she sneaks away from the campfire. This was a bug leftover from the old version of the game. It has been fixed.


- There were a couple obscure image files missing that wouldn't cause anything noticeable at first but it would trigger a looping check that would get worse and worse as the play session progressed. It would eventually bog down the game's code execution and cause problems in seemingly unrelated ways. This would sometimes later manifest as a soft-lock or a failed sprite load or a even cause certain animations or screen flashes to get skipped. 


- Certain enemies were dropping items from a discontinued loot table. This would manifest as receiving items marked by a red X. These enemies have had their loot tables corrected.


- There was a shop that sold the combat item Old Spellbook for 0 gold. Old Spellbooks are supposed to be a find-only item so they have been removed from that shop.


- There was a bug that was causing Natasha to go missing from the party on the map between the Imperial Camp and the balloon. This has been fixed.


- There was a treasure chest sitting rather conspicuously off to one side in the forest where Ogin and Gobsworth run with the worgs to find Natasha. When opened, it would show a "Phoenix Egg" card. This was an old treasure chest event from a long time ago. I have no idea how it got there or why I never noticed it before but it's gone now.


- I fixed several bugs over the past few weeks regarding the Vanessa character popping up when she's supposed to be elsewhere. I have now found the main source of this issue and fixed it.


- There was a problem with Eastpoint's entrance event not properly checking which way the player entered from. This has been fixed. The player character will now enter the Eastpoint map from the proper direction.


- The Misty Marshes outside Eastpoint were supposed to be a 1-time zone so that players wouldn't be subjected to a long walk every time they needed to leave Eastpoint from that side. This has been fixed. Players no longer have to travel through the Misty Marsh maps after completing it the first time.


- "[i]Your treasure hunter has returned. They didn't find anything this time.[/i]" This has been fixed. If you encountered this bug it was a result of accidentally triggering content from the planned Expansion Pack. There is a lot of work already done just in case I am able to reach my goal and continue development into the next game. This particular bug was manifesting in a very annoying way so I would like to apologize to any players who encountered it. If you see any of the following content in-game, please consider it a bug and report it as it is actually content meant for the next game: Anything to do with base building or hiring NPCs, class changing, dual-techs/triple-techs/etc, party swapping, or multiple inventories. I did this as a foresight to maintain player save file integrity even through multiple expansions.


- The fight with Gafgaren aboard the Imperial Ship was poor design on my part. To players who had leveled up enough by that encounter, it would not be apparent that Gafgaren could not be defeated at that time. This resulted in at least one player having their time wasted attempting to defeat him. To prevent any other players from suffering the same fate, and for the sake of better game design, the Gafgaren fight aboard the Imperial Ship has been re-designed as an in-battle scene rather than a fight the player is expected to lose.


- A bug was reported where a pathing route problem during the Bridge Troll scene would effectively soft-lock the game because the player character couldn't reach it's destination. After several attempts, I was not able to replicate this bug so I reworked the scene's pathing anyways just in case. I'm thankful for this report because it also made me realize there were some character emotes missing from the scene, making it feel sort of flat and bland (at least to me). So while I was doing the pathing I also added in some character emotes to inject a little more life into that scene.


- There were some incorrect character portraits for Bennett during the Klackoid Royal fight. These have been replaced with the correct image.




[u][b]Fixes Still in Progress[/b][/u]

- Still working on the sprint/dash redo. This hotfix had some stuff in it that took priority.





Just a reminder to all players! Sometimes Steam does not give an automatic update if it is too small. If ever in doubt, simply verify your game files. It will force an update, no matter how small, and you can be confident you have the most up-to-date version.

notes.title: Minor Update: Bug Fixes
notes.notes:
[u][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/u]

- There was a bug that allowed players to repeat the Old Hedge Wizard's magitech offer in the beginning of the game, making it possible to get unlimited Fire, Ice, and Lightning devices. This has been fixed.

- Some duplicate code was causing various Damage and Healing Over Time effects to trigger twice. This has been fixed.

- Fights in the forest just before reaching Marrick and Natasha's hometown no longer show just a black background image.

- Some typos and dialogue boxes have been fixed or updated.

- Players can no longer walk through walls after starting a New Game +

- The rage bar for bosses no longer shows up during the first few normal fights of a New Game +

[u][b]Temporary Changes - Fixes Still in Progress[/b][/u]

- The relic item "Casual Shoes" has been deactivated temporarily. This item was meant to allow players to move faster while walking through the game world but the code was checking for old character IDs so it wasn't working properly. When I fixed it, I realized it was activating even during cutscenes. This mechanic was coded almost 5 years ago and needs to be re-written. Players can expect a new sprint/dash feature in the next update.

- The looping animation effect for Auras has been temporarily disabled. All of the Aura skills still work, you just won't see the faded animation pulsing on the character projecting the Aura. This has been done for the sake of smoother combat performance during some of the more explosive visuals in later boss fights. On top of bug fixes, I am cleaning up and optimizing older parts of the game's code for better performance.

- There is an active bug report on Thaumetics sometimes un-equipping themselves after a character levels up at the end of a battle. When this happens, it can make it look like the character lost a stat point when leveling up when in fact it reflecting the stats lost from un-equipping the device. This bug is still being investigated.

- There is an active bug report in regards to how sometimes the player will enter a non-boss battle and all the enemies are already gone, granting the player a free win. I have located the source of this issue but did not have time to fix it today. This fix will be included in the next update along with the re-written sprint/dash.





Just a reminder to all players! Sometimes Steam does not give an automatic update if it is too small. If ever in doubt, simply verify your game files. It will force an update, no matter how small, and you can be confident you have the most up-to-date version.

notes.title: Ashen Roost Hotfix
notes.notes:
Marrick's Support Drone ability was registering as an "enemy heal" and would sometimes cause the friendly target to counter-attack or dodge the heal. This has been fixed.

There were some lighting issues on the topmost floors of the Old Dwarf Tower. These have been fixed.

notes.title: Error System Update
notes.notes:
The error handling system has been updated to be less austere. 

Rather than interrupting the player's game with an error message, bugs will now simply appear as glitches (unless it's something severe). If a bug occurs it will usually be completely unnoticeable. If it's a bigger bug there might be a small glitch hiccup or at worst the game may soft-lock until the player presses a button.

Also, there was an issue where the player could defeat Inquisitor Lugae, go downstairs, and walk out the front door. This would trigger another confrontation with Lugae, effectively trapping the player in a loop if they did not know where to go. This has been fixed.



Just a reminder to all players! Sometimes Steam does not give an automatic update if it is too small. If ever in doubt, simply verify your game files. It will force an update, no matter how small, and you can be confident you have the most up-to-date version.

notes.title: Inquisitor Lugae Hotfix
notes.notes: There was a bug that would sometimes crash the game after the Lugae fight under certain circumstances. This bug has been fixed.

notes.title: Ethni Hotfix
notes.notes:
Fixed an issue with Ethni's attack ability that was making it unusable.

Fixed an issue where the guide NPC sometimes wouldn't show up when choosing a branch.

notes.title: Logging Road Hotfix
notes.notes:
An old debugging event from the Early Access testing phase was toggling the save feature off while inside the Old Logging Road. This has been fixed. 

There was an image file corrupted in the encryption process that was causing a missing file error during battle encounters in the Old Logging Road. This has been fixed.

Some of the wandering encounters were triggering the wrong weather effects when their encounter was finished. These have been fixed.

notes.title: Small Update for Bug Fix
notes.notes:
There was an issue where players were allowed to walk back out into Gob-Gob's throne room after defeating him. This bug has been fixed.

Vanessa wasn't being added back to the party until a bit later. She now joins the party properly right after defeating Gob-Gob.

notes.title: Sticky Save Hotfix
notes.notes:
Just a quick hotfix to correct a bug found by our newest adventurer, the mighty Steverpg!



- When backing out of the game and reloading the save screen would sometimes stick for a long time or lock up completely. This has been fixed.

notes.title: Small Update with New Items
notes.notes:
The last couple updates have slightly changed how the player collects Magic Points to level up their Magitech devices. To adapt to the changes I have added in a couple new items that deal with Magic Points. Also, some new Magitech devices that were still in the experimental phase have been activated.



- Broken Magitech: a new item that can be salvaged for Scrap Materials, Thaumetic Parts, Mana Extract, or Upgrade Parts.

- Upgrade Parts: a new Item that grants up to 25 Magic Points to a character's current Magitech devices.

- Some new support devices are now available like Economizer MK-I which reduces the energy cost of skills from the linked device.

- Loot tables and shops around the world have been updated to accommodate these new items.

- There were some really old leftover events that were triggering old fights that didn't exist anymore. They have been updated with the proper encounters.

notes.title: Achievements & Magitech Hotfix
notes.notes:
Many thanks to Maddin for pointing out the problem with Steam Achievements! It led me down a rabbit hole of "uh-oh" that let me get ahead of some problems.



- Steam Achievements are fixed. For those who have been already playing, the game keeps track of achievement progress even without Steam's API so the next time you walk out onto the world map you should recieve any and all Steam Achievements you have already earned.

- There was an issue where the Magic Points a player gains after combat were returning a NAN value which could corrupt Magitech devices and cause them not to grow and level. This issue has been fixed but any Magitech devices that have already been corrupted may need to be replaced. Corrupted Magitech devices still work but they do not grow.

- Vanessa's ultimate was doing less damage than it was supposed to. This has been fixed.

- The Magitech Researchers in the first level that were displaying Lugae's sprite have been fixed.

- The end-of-battle UI was only showing skills learned if the player learned them at level up. The UI has been updated to show the player when they learn skills through Magitech devices or Blue Magic.

notes.title: Hotfix Patch
notes.notes:
First update with some hotfixes and adjustments:

- New Game + is now fully functional. Players that beat the game will be prompted at the end to create a New Game + file if they wish. New Game + lets you start the game from the beginning but with all your gold, gear, items, and levels from the previous game.

- The "Attack" command was using energy when it was not supposed to. This was causing "Attack" to get sealed out during exhaustion. This has been corrected.

- Some boss fights were still allowing players to run away and skip the fight. These have been fixed.

- The exhaustion effect was supposed to give energy regeneration but was instead taking energy away. This could leave a player in a bad spot if they didn't have any means of restoring energy quickly. This has been fixed.

notes.title: | Official Release |
notes.notes:
It's been a long road but I'm finally crossing the finish line.

With this update we are heading out of the Early Access phase and into the official release.

Thank you so much to everyone that showed their support by getting into the Early Access. I would especially like to thank Ceak from YouTube as well as Azuul, Revenge, and Maddin from here on Steam. Their testing and bug reports have been invaluable and seeing someone willing to play through multiple times gave me encouragement along the way.

There is good news and bad news with this release though... To get the bad news out of the way, the official release version breaks any and all old save files from Early Access test versions. I apologize for any inconvenience this might cause but I am hoping the results will be worth it. But that leads us to the good news!

I went all-out on this last update. There's a lot to go through but here is what's in the release:

- Updated and improved Magitech system

- New and updated skills and magic effects

- New and updated skill animations

- New and updated Steam Achievements

- Combat is now properly balanced

- New and updated weapons and armor database

- There are now 3 armor types up from 2 (light, general, heavy)

- HP gains per level have been increased to give player characters more health

- New and updated weapon graphics

- New weapon types available

- Updated monster database

- Updated gold, loot, and experience drops

- New and updated monster skills and attacks

- New and updated magitech devices

- New and updated trinkets and accessories

- Updated tooltips and descriptions

- Updated loot system to keep replays fresher. Many chests now offer randomized loot according to game progress

- Some new and updated animations have been added to story scenes

- Updated each character's Inner Fire ultimate attack

- Fixed some missing/wrong face graphics and character sprites

- Weather and Environment variables now work properly in combat (trigger storm, trigger cave-in, etc)

- The Blue Magic system has been updated

- Energy management in combat has been changed

- Combat skills now have mastery levels to make skills cost less and do more damage the more you use them

- The combat exhaustion mechanic has been re-balanced to match the new changes

- Some zone maps and scenes that felt bare have been touched up

- All secret basement locations have been updated

- Improvements to combat HUD and UI

- The Overworld system has been updated. Rare Monsters and Bandit Camps are now tied into the activated side content and Shipwrecks are no longer just battles every time

- Side content with the Monster Hunters and Mercenary Guild is now active


There's more I am forgetting but hopefully you can tell that there was a lot of work behind the decision to break old test files with the release version. The changes (especially the database re-writes) were just too much. Hopefully all the new goodies will make it worthwhile for anyone effected.


Some important things to note about the official release:

- You can no longer run away from boss fights
- You can still run away from other fights (except some certain story ones)
- You can no longer save inside dungeons except at save points
- The option to turn random encounters on and off still exists but it does not work while inside the final dungeon so use it wisely

notes.title: Pre-Release Combat Balancing
notes.notes:
I recently dropped a final test version update that I've been patching and hotfixing along the way. The combat was all over the place. Fine in some areas and wildly unbalanced in others. So on top of bug fixes I have been pouring effort into the combat.

This update contains massive changes to combat balancing:

- The entire database of skills, equipment, and enemies has been rebalanced.
- Character HP gain curve per level has been increased.
- Gold and experience gain has been updated.
- Magitech has been reworked so that it's spells are no longer just a copy of regular magic.
- Some new magitech devices have been added.
- Some new trinkets/accessories have been added.
- Characters now have 3 trinket slots. Up from 2.
- Magitech devices have had the spells they offer reworked.
- Magitech skills now have their own selection window in combat.
- Some new spells/skills and animations have been added.
- Blue Magic is up and running again.
- Some characters were starting with the wrong gear. That's been fixed.
- Ellessidel now starts with a Blue (ELF-II) device.
- Vanessa's dance mechanics have been reworked slightly.
- The attack chain combo has been expanded to include the new magitech.
- The attack chain combo has been changed slightly on a character by character basis. Characters now have 1 personal attack chain ability to add a little flavor and flair.
- Weapon images are now properly set.
- Tooltips on equipment and skills have been updated.
- Some boss fights were bugged. The Inquisitor Lugae fight was really buggy. This has been fixed.
- Side content has begun trickling in. A new Monster Hunter NPC can be found traveling around with information on rumors that will lead to optional side-bosses.
- Random overworld locations have been deactivated temporarily for reworking. (shipwrecks, bandit camps, etc)
- ...and much more! Too much to remember all at once here.

This update applies big changes to skills, gear, etc but it will not break any games already in progress. One or two magitech devices may suddenly be a different device but nothing beyond that. I apologize for any inconvenience.

Smoothing out the last wrinkles and running some tests to make sure the combat is good to go. After that, it's official release time! :D

notes.title: Final Early Access Test Version Live
notes.notes:
It's a little later than I intended but I feel like the results are worth it.

This is the final Early Access test version. I have uploaded it for stress testing while I clean it up for release.

The last version in the previous big update was missing a critical event that cut out a big important chunk of the game. This caused a rather confusing dropped plot point regarding  Andorlane and what was on the Data Rune. 

All scenes are now fully complete. No more wall-of-text placeholders. A few scenes have been reworked and a couple new scenes have been added in to strengthen and clarify aspects of the overall storyline.

The game is officially 100% playable from start to finish. All zones, all bosses, all scenes, etc through completion.

The amount of available save files has been increased from 10 to 20 save slots.

This will be the last version of the game to be released in "test mode". The official release version will not have the ability to save anytime, anywhere or let players run away from boss fights. Those features are only meant for Early Access testing.

Between now and release I will be focusing on bug hunting and combat balancing. I may also rearrange some of the treasure loot to reflect any balance changes in the skills or gear.

If you haven't played the game yet then be sure to boot it up at least once before release! The official release version will deactivate the ability to unlock the Early Access Steam Achievement. All you need to do is start the game. The achievement is activated as soon as a new game begins.

Thank you to everyone who has been a part of the development process! It has been a long and winding road to the finish line but it's finally within reach. I will be cleaning up loose ends, polishing up combat balancing, and answering any bug reports and then the final official release will launch.

notes.title: Major Update for 27 November 2024
notes.notes:
Neverspring Chronicles is [b]almost complete[/b]! This new major update is massive and stuffed full of bug fixes, performance improvements, new maps, new characters, polished scenes and more. To anyone who might be out there that has been playing the game as it develops, thank you for your support. It has been a long road and it feels very surreal to see light at the end of the tunnel.

[u][b]Major Update Notes[/b][/u]

[list]
[*] For testing purposes... all boss fights can be skipped by losing or running away. This will change on release.
[*] For testing purposes... players can save anytime, anywhere. This will change on release. (be careful saving at strange times like in the middle of a scene or event as it may cause problems if you try to load into the middle of something.)
[*] Several bugs and missing file errors have been fixed. Maps and coding have been cleaned up for better performance. So far in testing this seems to have fixed the problems with lag in towns.
[*] The planned Boss Fight mechanics have been implemented. Boss fights are now more bossy.
[*] All dungeons, levels, and map zones have been improved. Tons of new loot and secret treasures await.
[*] New characters have been introduced to adapt to changes in the storyline overhaul.
[*] Tutorial images have been peppered throughout early gameplay where appropriate.
[*] Inner Fire and character ultimates have been returned to the game.
[*] Incomplete or missing scenes have been fixed and polished.
[*] and more...
[/list]

[u][b]What's Left Until Release[/b][/u]

[list]
[*] Available gameplay will take you all the way to the last dungeon. At that point a notice will appear to the player warning them of spoiling the ending.
[*] The last dungeon is still under construction. It can be visited and explored but the monsters and sub-bosses are inactive. The treasure chests present are also just place holders.
[*] If a player ascends the final dungeon all the way to the top it will trigger the final confrontation and ending just as it is supposed to. However, while the ending dialogue is all written out completely through to the credits, the final boss fight is just a place holder (not the actual final boss fight) and the ending scenes are not polished with actor movement and eye candy.
[*] So all that being said... a player can test the game from start to finish and see how it all wraps up but it will not be as grand an experience as it will be when complete.
[*] Some things may change slightly as I finish up and polish the ending, though, so keep that in mind.
[*] Once I have completed the final dungeon, final boss fight, and polished up the end scenes then the game will be "complete" but I will still need to comb through it one last time to make sure everything is just right.
[*] I put the word "complete" in quotes like that because there is still one major part of the game's design that needs to be addressed during this last stretch of testing; balancing the combat formulas and gear progression.
[*] Finishing the physical map for the final dungeon won't take long. The biggest part of this last stretch is testing and balancing the combat and gear.
[/list]

[u][b]Stretch Goals[/b][/u]

[list]
[*] There are many things already coded into the game that I just need to build upon. Things I knew I wanted from the beginning but put off because I was focusing on actually getting the game finished.
[*] There is
[*] Combination Skills exist in the game (like Dual Techs and Triple Techs in Chrono Trigger) but I still need to actually make some skills for it.
[*] Side content like Villager Quests, Monster Hunting, and Mercenary Contracts exist in the game but are mostly deactivated while I polish them up.
[*] One or two more areas may be added, depending on how the flow of the game feels.
[*] Have you ever played games like Sid Meier's Civilization? You know how when you beat the game it gives you the option to keep playing? I have all this content sitting around from testing, research, and development... not to mention all the times the game went through complete overhauls... I really, really want to have it so that when the player beats the game for the first time it unlocks a whole other "Adventure Mode" that lets you play in the world as a sandbox. If you've ever played Sid Meier's Pirates! Gold then you might have an idea of what kind of sandbox play I'm talking about. No promises, though. It might be something I do in an update after release.
[/list]


Huge "thank you" to everyone that has helped me along the way by supporting this project's Early Access. Every little bit of feedback is appreciated. As I wrap things up and figure out the gear to combat balancing, now is the time for any "can you add in" or "wouldn't that be cool if". If you see any bugs or plot holes or confusing parts please don't hesitate to report whatever you find. I am working hard to get this project to release before Christmas! Thank you for your support.
